2026-08-27T04:27:38.7843775Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7843965Z 
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7844110Z To create a pull request:
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7844483Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7846868Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7848085Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7852895Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7855031Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7859208Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7860334Z 
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7866589Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7869911Z 
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7870987Z **Important**: `create_pull_request` is not a sandbox. Every successful call records a real PR intent that can become an externally visible pull request. 2026-08-27T04:27:38.7911531Z ```bash
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7912538Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7913055Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7913475Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7913784Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7914094Z ```
2026-08-27T04:27:38.7914905Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
